title: Get Moving
subtitle: Movement phase: disembark, move modes & the confirm gate

bullets: Click a unit's [Embarked] row to get the boys out of a transport — place each base inside the glowing ring. An attached Warboss gets out with them, so his base gets placed too.
Boyz that disembark can still make their own move — but only if the transport hasn't moved yet. Out first, drive after.
Movement modes: pick the radio button, then [b]Confirm Movement Mode[/b] — it doesn't stick till you confirm.
Drag models (or carry them with the pad), [b]Undo Model[/b] / [b]Reset Unit[/b] fix mistakes.
Big squad? Grab the whole lot in one go — [b]Select All[/b] on the keyboard, D-pad [b]▲[/b] on the pad — and one drag shifts them all.
You don't have to spend a move in one drag — drop, grab again, the inches add up till they're gone.
Turning a model is free in 11th — it doesn't cost a single inch of the move.
[b]End This Unit's Move[/b] locks one unit. The big red button ends the whole phase.

steps._comment: TWO beats in one step, and the second one was easy to miss: players shifted the mob and then sat there, because droppin' models looks finished. The step now says the confirm out loud in BOTH device bodies (the pad body never mentioned it at all), carries a live checklist whose second box stays open until the move is locked in, and uses anchor_when to walk the spotlight off the mob and onto End This Unit's Move the moment any model has staged distance.

steps._done_comment: The checklist is deliberately NOT the done gate: Remain Stationary is a legal way off this step and would never tick 'Shift da mob', so gating on the list would soft-lock that player. The boxes are the visible reminder, the any-tree is still the exit.

anchor_when.comment: models are down — point the ring at the button that finishes the move, the same one wagon_confirm spotlights later in the lesson

prompt.text: Advance adds a D6 to the move — and when a roll is this important, the game offers a [b]Command Re-roll[/b] (costs 1 CP). We're keeping it: click [b]Keep Roll[/b].
prompt.text_orky: Advance adds a D6 to da move — an' when a roll's dis important, da game offers a [b]Command Re-roll[/b] (costs 1 CP). We're keepin' it: click [b]Keep Roll[/b].

steps._comment: LOCK_MOVEMENT_MODE is allowed here even though this step is about the re-roll offer: MovementController._on_confirm_mode_pressed emits BEGIN_ADVANCE and then LOCK_MOVEMENT_MODE from the SAME click, and BEGIN_ADVANCE is what completes the previous step (wagon_mode) — synchronously, via PhaseManager.phase_action_taken -> _check_done. So by the time the second half of that one click reaches the gate, THIS step's allow-list is the one being consulted, and an empty list rejected it with 'tutorial_locked' the instant the player confirmed Advance.

rot0.comment: baseline facing on step entry — the wagon may already carry a rotation from deployment, so the done leaf compares against THIS, not against zero

done.comment: MovementController._apply_rotation_to_model writes the new facing straight into GameState (both Q/E and the pad's LB/RB, which PadRouter._synth_rotate turns into the same key events), so polling live state catches the turn the moment it happens — no action is dispatched for a rotation. 0.05 rad is a fifth of one 15-degree (PI/12 = 0.262 rad) tap, so a single press clears it and float noise cannot.

hint.kbm: You have to be holding the model — {key:rotate_left}/{key:rotate_right} do nothing when nothing is grabbed. Press and hold on the hull first, then tap them, then let go to drop it.

hint.pad: {lb}/{rb} turn the wagon any time its move isn't locked in yet — whether it's in your hand or parked where you dropped it. {a} on the hull picks it back up, {a} again drops it where it's pointing.
